pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Fix Extended Advertising channel use
pr_body:
Add implementation defined channel index in the auxiliary
pointer of the common extended payload format in the primary
channel PDUs and the same be used in the transmission of
auxiliary PDUs.

Fixes #35668.

Signed-off-by: Vinayak Kariappa Chettimada <vich@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: The channel selection of auxiliary advertisments in extended advertisments
issue_context.body:
Hi, is there any planned support for some heuristic functionality that would dynamically select channels for auxiliary advertisements? We found out that channel 0 is selected as the default for any extended advertising payloads which might be quite unreliable if there is a lot of inference on this particular channel.

Thanks,
Lukas
comments: Advertising extensions is work in progress, currently no one is working  is being done on the auxiliary advertising channels. Contributions to add it is welcome.
This shall be implemented before experimental label is removed for Advertising Extensions feature in Controller.

Just for information, current line length limit is 100 characters. 
At least I am sticking to that. Taking into account that I use clang-format to reorganize the code on my behalf, code written by me sticks to that limit.

This line isn't 100 characters though. 

80 is the recommendation, 100 is the max (which will be caught by CI afaik).

Yes it is just recommendation, so it is allowed to use longer line. 
What more Linux Kernel coding style does not enforce 100 characters either. It is a warning returned by kernel's checkpatch. Please see commit message in this PR: https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=bdc48fa11e46f867ea4d75fa59ee87a7f48be144.

What more I'm not asking to do a change, I'm just point that this kind of updates is optional and up to committer preferences.
Just curious: Is there a reason why you are using `+= 1U` instead of `first++`?
;-) or `++first` (in C it does not matter, but following general conventions this is the version of incrementation that should be used in situations `x = x + 1`)

> ;-) or `++first` (in C it does not matter, but following general conventions this is the version of incrementation that should be used in situations `x = x + 1`)

That's an old recommendation for old compilers though, right? 
IIRC a long time ago, `++i` and `i++` would result in different code, where `++i` would use one less register or something like that, but I think it's a long time since any reasonable compiler would do this.
Yes that is correct. I'm used to go for the pre-incrementation in situations like this.
Should we have an check or an ASSERT ensuring that `bdaddr` is non-NULL?
As the parameter was passed by internal module caller (hci.c or ull_scan.c) a NULL check branch can be avoided.

Correct me if I am wrong, but this function seems to return the address, as well as store it in the `bdaddr` argument, effectively "returning" it twice. 

Is this by design? It's similar to the memcpy/memset functions, so it's not necessarily wrong, just making sure it is intentional.
yes, it is by design, was simpler to return a valid pointer or NULL, compared to returning a errno.
